title.en: Frank Gunderson Joins Resonance as Academic Advisor

body.en:
Resonance: Journal of Global Music Studies is pleased to announce that Professor Frank Gunderson has joined the journal as an Academic Advisor.

Frank Gunderson is Professor of Musicology at Florida State University. He received the B.A. degree from Evergreen State College (WA), and the M.A. in World Music and Ph.D. in Ethnomusicology from Wesleyan University (CT). He has held previous appointments at Ohio University and University of Michigan, and he once taught for two years in a village Harambee secondary school in Kenya.

Gunderson’s research and teaching interests include musical intersections with Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) and sonic repatriation, African history, Islam, musical labor, veterans’ issues, biographical approaches, refugee communities, and documentary film. His research has been supported recently by Fulbright (Distinguished Chair Award, 2021-2022), and he has received awards from the National Endowment for the Humanities, Fulbright-Hays, and the Wenner-Gren Foundation.

Gunderson’s professional affiliations include the African Studies Association (ASA), the American Anthropological Association (AAA), and the Society for Ethnomusicology (SEM).

Gunderson was recently General Editor (2018-2022) of the SEM academic journal Ethnomusicology and is co-founder and co-Editor-in-Chief (together with Benjamin Harbert) of the new SEM Journal of Audiovisual Ethnomusicology. He has also served as the SEM Journal’s Film, Video, and Multimedia Review Editor, and has twice been a guest editor of the journal World of Music.

Gunderson has published more than fifty articles and reviews in Ethnomusicology, Africa Today, History and Anthropology, Soundings, and African Music, many of which can be found here. He has conducted extensive fieldwork in East Africa, and produced the recording Tanzania: Farmer Composers of North West Tanzania (1997, Multicultural Media) and co-edited with Gregory Barz the book Mashindano!: Competitive Music Performance in East Africa (2000, Mkuki na Nyota Press/African Books Collective LTD, Michigan State University Press). His book “We Never Sleep We Dream of Farming”: Sukuma Labor Songs from Western Tanzania (Brill Academic Press, 2010) was the 2009-2011 winner of the SEM Kwabena Nketia Book Award for best African music monograph. He co-edited with Robert Lancefield and Bret Woods The Oxford Handbook of Musical Repatriation (OUP 2018), and recently completed the dual biography, The Legacy of Tanzanian Musicians Muhidin Gurumo and Hassan Bitchuka – Rhumba Kiserebuka! (2018, Lexington Books/Rowman and Littlefield), which received Honorable Mentions from both the Alan Meriam Best Book prize committee (SEM) and the Best Book Prize committee of the International Council for Traditional Music.

Gunderson is an award-winning documentary filmmaker. While music director of KAOS radio in Olympia, WA, he worked with his cousin, the Northwest “outsider” musician Travis Roberts, on a project that culminated in several high-profile indie recordings as well as an award-winning film co-directed with Bret Woods called Human Skab (SnagFilms, 2012). His recent film about a Tanzanian drum-maker, Ng’oma: The Work of Our Clan (Alexander Street / Ethnographic Video Online, 2020), has been shown in dozens of film festivals worldwide. His most recent film project, “Beloved Youth of Many Days”: Stories about Mlimani Park Orchestra, has been accepted into fifty international film festivals and is distributed by the Royal Anthropological Institute.

Resonance: Journal of Global Music Studies is committed to fostering cross-cultural, transregional, and interdisciplinary dialogue in global music studies. Professor Gunderson’s experience in ethnomusicology, African music research, sonic repatriation, audiovisual scholarship, musical labor, and academic publishing will provide valuable guidance as the journal continues to develop its scholarly community.

We warmly welcome Professor Frank Gunderson to the Academic Advisory Board of Resonance.

title.en: Call for Papers: Volume 1 of Contemporary Review of Political Thought

body.en:
Contemporary Review of Political Thought (CRoPT) is now inviting submissions for its first volume. The journal welcomes original scholarly work in English or Chinese.

Contemporary Review of Political Thought（CRoPT，《当代政治思想评论》）现面向学界征集第一卷稿件。本刊欢迎英文或中文原创学术论文投稿。

CRoPT is an international, peer-reviewed, open-access online academic journal dedicated to the study of political thought, political philosophy, intellectual history, Marxist theory, ideological and political education, higher education governance, and modern public life.

CRoPT 是一本国际性、同行评审、开放获取的在线学术期刊，关注政治思想、政治哲学、智识史、马克思主义理论、思想政治教育、高等教育治理与现代公共生活等领域。

We welcome submissions that engage with political concepts, theoretical traditions, institutional change, public values, democracy, justice, power, sovereignty, freedom, equality, rights, citizenship, public reason, legitimacy, modernity, globalization, social movements, public life, technological change, and contemporary political imagination.

本刊欢迎围绕政治概念、思想传统、制度变迁、公共价值、民主、正义、权力、主权、自由、平等、权利、公民身份、公共理性、合法性、现代性、全球化、社会运动、公共生活、技术变迁与当代政治想象等主题展开的研究。

投稿稿件须为原创、未发表且未一稿多投。稿件建议使用可编辑 Word 文件，并包含摘要、关键词、正文、注释、参考文献及必要的表格、图示、附录和相关声明。

Research articles, theoretical essays, review articles, policy and institutional analyses, and special issue articles are normally subject to double-blind peer review. Forum contributions, book reviews, invited pieces, and shorter texts may be assessed through editorial review, peer review, or a mixed process, depending on the nature of the submission.

研究论文、理论论文、综述论文、政策与制度分析及专题论文通常采用双盲同行评审。论坛文章、书评、约稿或短文可根据稿件性质采用编辑评审、同行评审或混合评审流程。

Authors are invited to submit manuscripts through the journal’s online submission system. Please read the Author Guidelines before submission and ensure that all required metadata and declarations are completed accurately.

title.en: Call for Papers for the September Issue: AI, Climate Sustainability, and Environmental Transformation

body.en:
Climate Sustainability & Global Systems (CSGS) invites submissions for its regular September issue.

As artificial intelligence continues to develop rapidly, new opportunities are emerging to improve climate research, environmental monitoring, sustainability transitions, and global systems governance. At the same time, AI applications in climate and environmental research require methodological transparency, ethical responsibility, data integrity, reproducibility, and careful consideration of social, ecological, and policy implications.

For the September issue, CSGS particularly welcomes high-quality submissions that explore how responsible AI, environmental data science, modeling, and digital technologies can contribute to climate sustainability, environmental protection, resilience building, and systemic risk analysis.

Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:

• AI applications in climate modeling, Earth system analysis, and environmental prediction• Machine learning for environmental monitoring, pollution assessment, and ecosystem protection• AI-assisted approaches to climate risk assessment, adaptation planning, and resilience building• Data-driven tools for carbon management, energy transitions, and sustainable infrastructure• Responsible AI for sustainability governance, climate policy, and decision-making• Remote sensing, geospatial analysis, and AI for land, water, biodiversity, and urban systems• AI-based early warning systems for extreme weather, disasters, and systemic climate risks• Socio-ecological impacts of AI-enabled climate and environmental technologies• Equity, justice, transparency, and accountability in AI-driven sustainability solutions• Interdisciplinary frameworks linking AI, climate science, sustainability transitions, and global governance

In addition to AI-related submissions, the journal continues to welcome manuscripts across its broader scope, including climate systems modeling, sustainability governance, global climate policy, socio-ecological resilience, climate-economy systems, and interdisciplinary methods and analytical frameworks.

CSGS welcomes original research articles, review articles, policy analysis papers, methods and frameworks papers, short communications, and data- or AI-focused reports that align with the journal’s aims and scope.

All submissions should present rigorous methods, clear academic English, transparent data and code practices where applicable, and strong relevance to climate sustainability and global systems. Authors using AI tools in text preparation, data processing, coding, modeling, visualization, or image generation must include an appropriate AI Use Statement in the manuscript. Data Availability, Funding, and Conflict of Interest statements are also required.

Manuscripts should be submitted through the journal’s official submission system. Authors are encouraged to review the Author Guidelines, Data Policy, AI & Research Integrity Policy, and Publication Ethics Requirements before submission.

For inquiries, please contact the Editorial Office at:

csgs@panorama-sg.com

Climate Sustainability & Global Systems looks forward to receiving rigorous, transparent, and globally relevant research that advances understanding and action at the intersection of climate sustainability, environmental transformation, and global systems.

title.en: Call for Papers for the December 2026 Issue: Circulating Sounds: Translation, Mediation, and Publics in Global Music Studies

body.en:
Resonance: Journal of Global Music Studies invites submissions for its December 2026 issue.

Circulating Sounds: Translation, Mediation, and Publics in Global Music Studies

Music is not merely recorded, performed, preserved, or interpreted as a stable work. It is also transformed as it moves across languages, media, platforms, institutions, and listening communities. A translation, a cross-media adaptation, a recording or livestream of a performance, or a renewed act of listening may place music in a different context and generate new meanings.

For the December 2026 issue, we particularly welcome contributions engaging with the theme “Circulating Sounds: Translation, Mediation, and Publics in Global Music Studies.” Submissions on other topics within the broader scope of the journal are also welcome.

This issue invites reflection on how music is reinterpreted, reorganized, and reused through processes of circulation, and on how these processes shape audiences, media practices, forms of knowledge, and cultural politics. In recent years, musicology, ethnomusicology, popular music studies, media studies, translation studies, and area studies have increasingly examined music as a mobile cultural practice shaped by technologies, institutions, markets, platforms, and publics.

We welcome submissions addressing, but not limited to, the following topics:

• the translation of lyrics, titles, terms, musical concepts, and theoretical categories;• musical adaptation and reinterpretation across film, theatre, short video, games, exhibitions, digital art, and other media forms;• the recording, filming, livestreaming, archiving, and platform circulation of live performance;• the transnational movement of local sounds, traditional musics, popular music, and experimental sound practices;• the role of digital platforms, algorithmic recommendation, social media, and streaming infrastructures in musical circulation and reception;• the ways translation, mediation, and circulation reshape musicological writing, source selection, analytical methods, and knowledge production;• historical, ethnographic, sociological, linguistic, archival, and practice-based approaches related to the above issues.

Submissions should present a clearly articulated research question, strong engagement with relevant scholarship, and a well-defined methodology. Articles are expected to be grounded in concrete materials, cases, fieldwork, texts, archives, media practices, or creative practice, and to contribute to broader debates in global music studies.

The journal accepts submissions in English, Chinese, German, Italian, and Russian. All manuscripts must include an English title and abstract. Manuscripts should follow the journal’s submission guidelines and Chicago citation style.

Submissions and inquiries may be sent to:rjgms.editorial@panorama-sg.com

title.en: Important Notice: Double-Blind Peer Review and Similarity Report Requirements

body.en:
Dear Authors,

To further enhance the academic standards and publication quality of the Health Nexus: Interdisciplinary Medical Research Journal, we are strictly enforcing the following submission requirements. Please read and comply with these guidelines carefully before submitting your manuscript:

1. Strict Double-Blind Peer Review We employ a rigorous double-blind peer review process. To ensure complete anonymity and objective evaluation, authors MUST upload their submission as two separate documents:

A Separate Title Page: This document must contain the manuscript title, complete names and affiliations of all authors, corresponding author contact details, funding declarations, acknowledgments, and conflict of interest statements.

An Anonymized Main Manuscript: This document is the only text sent to reviewers and must not contain any identifying author information. Authors must ensure that self-citations are blinded (e.g., replace citations with "[Author citation deleted for peer review]") and that all author-identifying metadata is removed from the document properties.

2. Mandatory Similarity Report (<15%) We maintain a zero-tolerance policy towards plagiarism and academic misconduct. All new submissions must be accompanied by a full, official similarity report, uploaded as a supplementary file in the system:

Accepted Tools: We require official, full-text reports (in PDF format) generated by recognized academic authorities, such as Turnitin or iThenticate.

Threshold: The total Similarity Index must be strictly below 15%. Please note that even if the total score is below 15%, the Editorial Office reserves the right to reject the manuscript if the similarity rate from a single source is disproportionately high.

*Notice of Non-Compliance: Submissions that fail to provide a completely anonymized main manuscript or lack a compliant official similarity report (<15%) will not enter the peer-review process and will be returned to the author immediately during the initial screening phase.

Thank you for your understanding, cooperation, and continued support of our academic standards.

Editorial Office, Health Nexus

title.en: Editorial Announcement: Author Submission Requirements / 编辑公告：作者投稿与出版政策说明

body.en:
This journal draws inspiration from the scholarly tradition of Silence (Springer Nature, ISSN: 1758-907X), which focused on interdisciplinary studies of silence. The original journal has now been archived and no longer accepts new submissions. Previously published articles remain accessible through the Springer Nature Link platform and other academic databases.

Building on this intellectual tradition, this journal continues the exploration of silence and related themes while developing its own editorial framework and research perspectives. The journal serves as an independent platform for reflective, interdisciplinary, and experimental scholarship.

The journal particularly encourages research that engages with intellectual reflection, methodological transparency, and evolving research processes. In addition to conventional research articles, the journal also welcomes reflective and experimental academic formats through sections such as Quiet Research, Silence Notes, Failed Experiments, Unwanted Reviews, Void Dialogue, and Null Reviews.

Submission Requirements

Authors submitting manuscripts should ensure that their work follows standard academic writing conventions and includes the basic components of scholarly articles, such as title, abstract, keywords, main text, and references. Submissions that do not meet basic academic or formatting standards may be returned for revision before editorial evaluation.

Authorship Policy

The journal no longer publishes anonymous articles. While some earlier materials may have appeared without complete authorship information, these historical publications will remain unchanged. All future submissions must include accurate author names, institutional affiliations, and contact information.

Academic Integrity

All submissions must follow principles of academic integrity. Manuscripts may undergo editorial screening for plagiarism or other forms of academic misconduct. Submissions involving plagiarism, duplicate publication, or unethical practices will be rejected.

By submitting a manuscript, authors confirm that they have read and agreed to the journal’s policies and submission requirements.

本刊在学术理念上受到 Springer Nature 出版期刊 Silence（ISSN: 1758-907X）的研究传统启发。该期刊曾关注“沉默”及其相关跨学科研究，目前已归档并停止接收新的投稿，其已发表文章仍可通过 Springer Nature Link 及相关学术数据库进行浏览与引用。

在这一学术传统基础上，本刊继承并延续与“沉默研究”相关的研究方向，同时发展自身的编辑框架与研究视角。本刊作为一个独立学术平台，鼓励跨学科、反思性以及具有探索性的学术研究。

除常规学术论文外，本刊还通过多个栏目支持不同形式的学术探索，包括 Quiet Research、Silence Notes、Failed Experiments、Unwanted Reviews、Void Dialogue 和 Null Reviews 等。

投稿要求

作者投稿应遵循规范的学术写作标准，并包含论文的基本结构，如标题、摘要、关键词、正文和参考文献。不符合基本学术或格式要求的稿件，编辑部可能在进入编辑评估前退回作者修改。

作者署名政策

本刊不再接受匿名发表。早期部分已发表内容可能未完整标注作者信息，这些历史内容将保持原状。但从现在开始，所有投稿必须提供真实完整的作者姓名、所属机构及联系方式。

学术诚信

所有投稿必须遵守学术诚信原则。编辑部可能对稿件进行查重与学术规范审核。如发现抄袭、一稿多投或其他学术不端行为，稿件将被拒绝。

作者提交稿件即表示已阅读并同意遵守本刊的投稿与出版政策。

title.en: Call for Papers | “开盒”与青少年数字暴力：法律回应、心理机制与传播责任 / Doxxing and Digital Violence Against Adolescents: Legal Responses, Psychological Mechanisms, and Media Responsibility

body.en:
征稿启事｜《法律·心理学·传播研究学刊》2026年第二卷第二期

近年来，“开盒”作为一种数字暴力行为在青少年社交平台上频发，其带来的心理创伤、隐私侵犯与法律失序问题日益引发社会关注。青少年作为网络环境中的高敏感群体，亟需从法律制度、心理支持与媒介治理层面获得系统回应。

本刊2026年第二卷第二期将以“‘开盒’与青少年数字暴力：法律回应、心理机制与传播责任”为专题，欢迎以跨学科视角探讨以下方向（包括但不限于）的高质量稿件投稿：

青少年为何成为“开盒”对象？心理机制与社会认知分析

“开盒”行为的法律界定与责任追究（刑法/民法/平台治理）

媒体与社交平台在青少年隐私保护中的伦理责任

“开盒”对青少年心理健康的影响：创伤、羞耻与社会退缩

“开盒”传播路径、情绪感染机制与网络群体行为研究

国际比较：“doxxing”在不同法律体系下的监管策略

法律教育与青少年网络自我保护能力的建构

案例研究：典型“开盒”事件中的法律、心理与传播干预

投稿截止日期：2026年4月15日预计出版时间：2026年7月（Vol. 2 No. 2）接受文种：中文或英文（均需具备学术规范）投稿方式：请通过期刊官网投稿系统提交投稿页面：https://grhas.centraluniteduniversity.de/index.php/jlpcs/about/submissions

Call for Papers｜Journal of Law, Psychology, and Communication Studies Vol. 2 No. 2 (2026)

The widespread occurrence of “doxxing” — the act of publicly exposing personal information — on social media platforms has led to increasing concerns over adolescent mental health, privacy violations, and the blurred boundaries of digital legality. As vulnerable participants in digital spaces, adolescents require nuanced, interdisciplinary protection through law, psychology, and media governance.

This special issue (Vol. 2 No. 2) invites original research contributions that address the theme:“Doxxing and Digital Violence Against Adolescents: Legal Responses, Psychological Mechanisms, and Media Responsibility”

Suggested topics include (but are not limited to):

Why are adolescents often targeted in doxxing? Psychological mechanisms and social cognition

Legal definitions and accountability of doxxing in civil and criminal contexts

The ethical responsibilities of platforms in protecting minors’ privacy

Psychological impact of online exposure: trauma, shame, and social withdrawal

Spread mechanisms and emotional contagion in doxxing communication

Cross-cultural analysis of doxxing regulations and digital rights

Legal education and adolescent self-protection in online environments

Case studies of interventions: legal, psychological, and communicative perspectives

Dear authors and researchers,

AI & Future Society (ISSN: 3053-4011) is now accepting submissions for Volume 2, Issue 1 (May 2026).

Submission deadline: April 15, 2026

This is a regular issue of the journal.There are no Article Processing Charges (APC) for this issue.

The editorial theme of Volume 2, Issue 1 (May 2026) is:

AI, Algorithmic Thresholds, and Social Fairness:AI Systems, Social Theory, Ethics, Economics, and Public Policy Governance in the Context of the U.S. Middle-Class “Cut-Off Line” Debate

In recent years, AI-driven decision systems have increasingly relied on algorithmic thresholds, scoring mechanisms, and cut-off points in areas such as social welfare, healthcare, credit evaluation, education access, taxation, and housing policy.

Public debates—particularly in the United States—have highlighted how these threshold-based systems may contribute to the structural exclusion of middle-income and near-threshold populations, often described in public discourse as a “middle-class cut-off line.”

This issue encourages submissions that critically examine:

AI-driven threshold and scoring systems as socio-technical arrangements

The interaction between algorithmic decision-making and social stratification

Ethical issues related to fairness, responsibility, and accountability

Economic rationales embedded in algorithmic governance

Public policy and regulatory responses to AI-mediated exclusion

Contributions may draw on social theory, ethics, economics, public policy, law, or interdisciplinary approaches.

As a regular open-topic issue, submissions are welcome on the above theme as well as on other topics, provided they align with one of the journal’s core sections:
